title: Forgotten Forms in Babylonian Aramaic (Mandaic and Jewish)
publisher: Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel Institute of Jewish Studies, Hebrew University of Jerusalem; distributed by Magnes Press
citation: Morgenstern, Matthew. ‘Forgotten Forms in Babylonian Aramaic (Mandaic and Jewish)’ [Hebrew]. Mehqarim be-Lashon 20 (2023): 171–194.
notes: Complete article inspected in the researcher-supplied 298-page volume, SHA-256 2d087410e67656b16aa7e92468e8c0e78149edc671c285bb280d24416f741dcd. A linguistic study drawing extensively on published and unpublished Jewish Babylonian Aramaic and Mandaic bowls; it is not an object edition. Its four case studies concern the 2 f.s. imperfect ending -ay, Mandaic -h for the 3 f.s. suffix, apocope of word-final n in pre-classical Mandaic pronominal suffixes, and 2 f.pl. participles based on qāṭlān-.
